default.note: The shipped field battle: Campus Martius, ultra order of battle, quality=high, 8,632 men. Recorded at 88a4aa5. Re-record only in the same commit as the change that moved it. ||| Re-recorded by the determinism-cliff pass, and this one is a re-record of the FORMAT rather than of the battle. Two things changed. (1) Two checkpoints added past t+200: the gate used to stop 5.5 s before the only cross-engine divergence anyone has measured (the field battle forks at t+205.5 s), so t+250 is the sentinel just past the fork and t+400 is the second half of the battle nothing had ever looked at. (2) Two new marks per checkpoint. `uf64` is the exact float64 bits of every continuous UnitGroupState field plus the waypoint queue — the layer the float32 pool hash cannot see, and which nothing in this repository hashed until now. `uctl` is the discrete half: order, target, formation, width, alive, kills, membership, flags, and unit array order. The five original pool hashes are UNCHANGED at all three battles across the whole pass, including across the Math.hypot -> Math.sqrt(a*a + b*b) substitution in the same branch, and so are all 21 survivor counts. Every `uf64` moved, and no `uctl` did: the substitution perturbs the simulation own float64 state everywhere, never reaches a control-flow decision, and never survives the float32 round trip. That is the quantisation firewall, and it is why the old five-checkpoint pool-only gate would have reported that a 222-call-site change did nothing. A `uf64` drift with `hash` and `uctl` unchanged is a PORTABILITY finding — a browser update is enough to cause one — and the gate warns rather than fails on it. A `uctl` or `hash` drift is a real change in the battle and still fails. Recorded from three independent page loads per battle, cross-checked against an earlier independent pair of runs: all 21 checkpoints reproduced exactly. Headcounts 8,632 / 3,074 / 3,440 confirm each arm measured the battle it names. ||| Re-recorded by the pass that put the field deployment on its own ground, and this one IS a re-record of the battle. `sim/scenario.ts` laid both lines out about x 0 and never read the deployment masks; §15 task 1 moved those masks east with the corrected Tiber and left the order of battle where it was, so at 70fc191 **747 of these 8,632 men were standing in the river** and another 412 were dry on the far bank, in the wrong battle. Measured with `tools/probe-ground.mjs --quality=high --views=none`, which now audits the men as well as the ground. The deployment is now translated once onto the axis the masks define — one shift of 271.146 m for every unit of both armies, so frontage (Rome 684.3 m, the host 783.4 m), spacing, width, facing, formation, unit count and headcount are identical to the metre before and after; only x moved. In water 747 -> 0, far bank 412 -> 0, worst slope under a man 0.529 -> 0.315. The battle that follows is a different battle for the obvious reason: an army that was fighting with its left wing in a river is not the same army. Survivors at t+400 move 5,217 -> 4,288. The previous pin was already red at 70fc191 for a different reason — the terrain pass at c44ded0 moved the ground under this battle and deliberately did not re-record it, on the grounds that pinning it would pin a broken battle. Measured at 70fc191 in a separate worktree, for the record: t+0 0fa6e702, then ee0f62b6, d343cc70, 3d79f110, 8ebc59fe, 7b951be2, 233e3022. Recorded from three independent page loads, all bit-identical at all seven checkpoints on hash, uf64 and uctl. One mark says the composition claim better than any prose can: **`uctl` at t+0 is 2b2ac282 and at t+30 is 13f5b86e, which are the values recorded at 88a4aa5**, before the terrain moved and before this. The discrete half — order, target, formation, width, alive, kills, membership, flags and unit array order — is byte-identical to the battle that shipped. Only the continuous half moved, and only in x.

Every one of those moves the ground the storm crosses and the masonry it crosses it toward, so every checkpoint drifted and all seven were expected to. **The two controls are bit-identical across the same tree**, measured on the same dev server minutes before this was recorded: `default` UNCHANGED at all seven checkpoints at 8,632 soldiers, and `map=carthage&scenario=assault` UNCHANGED at all seven at 3,440. Headcount here is 3,074, which is the tell that this arm measured Rome. A and B agree on every bit at all seven checkpoints across two independent page loads. Tasks 6-14 rebuild this wall further and each of them owns its own re-record.
